players.product: US T&D contractor - Hyosung HICO Breaker JV partner (US gas circuit breakers)

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 2026 results (CFO Jayshree Desai): revenues of $7.9 billion, net income attributable to common stock of $221 million or $1.45 per diluted share, adjusted diluted EPS of $2.68 and adjusted EBITDA of $686 million, with record $48.5 billion of backlog. Duke Austin: robust double-digit growth in revenues, adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EPS; 'we're at 30% EPS growth with no acquisitions in the quarter.' Seasonality is changing - 'The first quarter, you know, it doesn't fall off as much' - as fabrication and pre-manufacturing take risk out of field work.
quarterly_data.figure: Revenue $7.9 billion; net income $221 million / $1.45 per diluted share; adj EPS $2.68; adj EBITDA $686 million; record $48.5 billion backlog; 30% EPS growth with no acquisitions

quarterly_data.signal: FY2026 guidance raised on the record backlog, strong Q1 and improved visibility: revenues $34.7 billion-$35.2 billion, adjusted EBITDA $3.49 billion-$3.65 billion, adjusted EPS $13.55 and $14.25. Duke Austin: guidance includes no acquisitions ('We made no acquisitions in the first quarter, and that's what the guidance is'); any future deals will be added, and he expects M&A over the next nine months. Free cash flow guidance left unchanged, but CFO has 'greater confidence about being at the higher end of that cash flow range.' Longer-term: Investor Day (March 31st) outlined an opportunity to more than double earnings power by 2030, a 15%-20% adjusted EPS growth target, and a $2.4 trillion addressable market converging around utility, generation and large load.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 revenue $34.7 billion-$35.2 billion; adj EBITDA $3.49 billion-$3.65 billion; adj EPS $13.55 and $14.25; 15%-20% adjusted EPS growth target; $2.4 trillion TAM

quarterly_data.signal: VERTICAL SUPPLY CHAIN FOR GRID EQUIPMENT. Duke Austin: the $500 million-$700 million investment announced on the Q4 call in power transformer manufacturing 'will double our power transformer manufacturing capacity'; off-site manufacturing, fabrication and logistics facilities are nearly doubling to approximately 6.7 million sq ft, with 'significant demand for these services, particularly for data centers.' On interconnection delays: 'the transformer manufacturing investment matters a ton when you start talking about 36 months on transformers', with European inbounds 'held up overseas' - 'We've really de-risked the transformer piece of that.' Quanta is 'the top five buyer of HV equipment', which lets it negotiate programs on a total-cost basis.
quarterly_data.figure: $500 million-$700 million transformer investment doubles transformer capacity; approximately 6.7 million sq ft of facilities; 36 months on transformers

quarterly_data.signal: Backlog build was broad-based, not one big award (Duke Austin): 'The first, like, meaningful 765 that came in. It was less than 25% of the B, so, you know, call it less than $1 billion in there. It was an MSA type over a multi-year period that can grow and expand, not with the client that we've discussed.' Generation is still outside backlog: 'None of the CGT or even any of the generation for the most part that's been announced is not in our backlog'; as air permits progress it should come into backlog 'probably the later half of the year and beyond.' The CGT business 'could be substantial, and they are chunky' - 'you'll see the company stack in the back half and beyond.' Management expects backlog to keep rising year-over-year.
quarterly_data.figure: 765 kV MSA less than 25% of the backlog increase (less than $1 billion); generation work not yet in backlog

quarterly_data.signal: Gas generation and the long cycle. Duke Austin: 'You're seeing orders out on combined cycle engines into 2030' and CGTs take 3 years to build once they hit the ground, so 'you're in 2033 at a minimum on the orders you get today'; he sees demand 'for a decade plus.' Quanta is comfortable on single-cycle plants but prudent on combined-cycle risk; inbound calls are daily and the business was built organically. On the NiSource program (an analyst cited $5.7 billion) he said '5.7 that's growing every day.' On bridge power: 'there's Bloom and others that we're involved with on jobs', but the 'vast majority are going to the grid at some point.'
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure (combined-cycle orders into 2030; CGTs take 3 years to build; 2033 at a minimum)

quarterly_data.signal: Technology / large-load end market. Duke Austin, on the raised technology and load-center outlook: 'We are looking at 100-plus % growth in it, due to acquisition, due to strategy'; organic growth is also strong; technology is 'a, you know, trillion plus TAM'; 'we've only been doing this, like, a year and a half.' Prefab / pre-manufactured product (a Cupertino strength) is 'MSA type driven programmatic spend against the AI build, both cloud-based and learning-based type products' rather than chunky projects. Quanta already does some balance-of-plant data centers and could do full builds at scale with added people; it has '2,000 plus engineers internally.' Load is 'real' and 'not just AI' - onshoring of chips and robotics also drive it.
quarterly_data.figure: 100-plus % growth in technology outlook; trillion plus TAM; 2,000 plus engineers

quarterly_data.signal: Craft labour build (Duke Austin): 'We added, you know, relatively 5,000 to 6,000 organically last year, and we'll do that again this year plus.' M&A is 'not a labor strategy'; acquisitions remain the primary use of capital. End markets show no holes; Iran war / higher diesel is 'such a little piece of our spend' and the supply chain 'looks good.' Canada: pipe-side awards expected over the next few quarters; margins picking up but not yet at parity with the U.S.
quarterly_data.figure: 5,000 to 6,000 craft workers added organically last year

contracts.signal: Duke Austin: 'We have a great relationship with AEP. As they announce 765, we're right in the middle of it with them, both on equipment as well as.' Quanta put its equipment investment in the script 'to show you that we're moving forward on significant dollars against that 765 build in the vertical supply chain'; a U.S.-based supply chain de-risks Quanta and AEP and 'has led to work and great opportunities together across the board on their system.' 'We're just getting started.'
